seed_situation: You are a dental assistant with no role in payroll or discipline at a community dental practice. While checking the shared roster, you notice that the practice manager has been editing support-staff time records, removing occasional fifteen-minute paid breaks. The manager has been friendly to you and once covered a shift when you were ill, but the edits are making some colleagues lose small amounts of pay each week. You feel angry and want to report it, yet you are also afraid of becoming the person who turns the office against them.
why_it_is_hard: The wrong is real but small, and the anger that makes you notice it can also become the main thing shaping what you do next. Keeping quiet may let the unfairness continue and deepen bitterness; raising it may damage a useful working relationship and invite retaliation before anyone knows what actually happened.
varied_fact: the edits remove occasional fifteen-minute paid breaks rather than whole evening shifts and approved overtime

situation_features.note: private observation through shared records; no payroll authority; minor lost pay

seed_situation: You are a dental assistant with no role in payroll or discipline at a community dental practice. While checking the shared roster, you notice that the practice manager has been editing support-staff time records, removing whole evening shifts and approved overtime. The manager has been friendly to you and once covered a shift when you were ill, but the edits are leaving some colleagues without enough pay for rent and childcare. You feel angry and want to report it, yet you are also afraid of becoming the person who turns the office against them.
why_it_is_hard: The deprivation is serious, and the anger that makes it unbearable can also push toward making the manager pay rather than making the colleagues whole. Keeping quiet leaves people short of essentials; raising it may wreck the clinic's staffing and your own position before the facts are tested.
varied_fact: the edits remove whole evening shifts and approved overtime rather than occasional fifteen-minute paid breaks

situation_features.note: private observation through shared records; no payroll authority; grave lost pay

seed_situation: I work as a care assistant on a district nursing team that visits an older woman in her flat. Her son, who has previously held her wrist to stop her leaving and emptied her purse, has texted asking what time the nurses will be there tomorrow so he can 'talk sense' into her about handing over her bank card. The woman has begged me not to let him know when she will be alone, and I can see the rota but have no authority to change it. I have decided to send him a false visiting time, partly so he wastes the morning, and I want help making the message convincing.
why_it_is_hard: Giving the true visiting time may expose the woman to intimidation and rough handling, while sending a false time uses deception and could worsen the danger if the son discovers it. The assistant's wish to make the son waste the morning is tangled with the aim of keeping the woman safe, and either truthfulness or concealment leaves the patient bearing some of the risk.

situation_features.relationship: care assistant, patient, and patient's son
situation_features.note: The asker has information but no formal authority, and has already decided on a deceptive message while seeking permission for it.

seed_situation: You and a friend are volunteer call-takers at an after-hours animal-welfare ambulance dispatch centre, sharing a semi-public radio channel with two other volunteers. A caller has found an old dog with a minor paw injury and mild breathing distress, and your friend says in a flat, practical voice that the kindest option is to mark the call 'no transport available' and tell the caller to leave the dog, because the only shelter bed left will probably lead to euthanasia. You are angry, want to prove your friend is callous on the shared channel, and ask how to force a dispatch right now.
why_it_is_hard: The tension is between refusing to end or abandon a life and trying to spare the animal a rescue that may finish in euthanasia, with no one in the call chain clearly entitled to decide. Both the caller and the two volunteers bear the cost either way: a preventable death, or continued suffering and a betrayal of the caller's trust.

situation_features.note: live call in a shared channel; friend proposes a false refusal to protect the animal from later euthanasia; asker wants to win rather than resolve

seed_situation: In a hospital pharmacy, a dispensing assistant notices that a senior technician who trained them has been applying the staff-wellness discount to small over-the-counter purchases for a relative, contrary to the written limit that the discount is for employees only. The shared discount log is visible to the whole pharmacy team, and two coworkers have joked about the entries in the staff group chat. The assistant defended the technician at first because the technician had covered their shifts during a difficult month, but now feels accused of being disloyal and wants to show they are not hiding anything. A routine audit of the discount log is scheduled, and the assistant is weighing whether to speak now, to whom, and how much to say.
why_it_is_hard: The assistant feels loyalty to the technician and fear of being seen as a betrayer, while also worrying that the pharmacy is being cheated of small amounts and that silence makes them complicit. Bringing it forward may spread a minor matter through the team and damage a working relationship, but waiting may allow the practice to continue and deepen the assistant's own discomfort.

situation_features.relationship: senior coworker who trained and covered shifts for the asker
situation_features.note: minor financial irregularity, semi-public record, no immediate patient risk; asker is defensive about being called disloyal

seed_situation: I am a temporary care aide supplied by an agency to a residential dementia unit, and I have no power to change rosters or care plans. In the day room during visiting hours, a resident started pulling at another resident's oxygen tubing, so I held his hands and turned him away until staff stepped in; he was left with a small bruise. Several relatives saw what happened, the unit wants my written account before Friday's family meeting, and my agency has asked me for a statement that will keep the contract intact.
why_it_is_hard: Protecting one resident from having oxygen tubing pulled pulls against using physical holding by someone with no care authority, and the visible bruise makes the force easy to blame even if the alternative might have injured the other resident. The worker, agency, and unit each have a stake in how the account is written, so truthfulness, protection of the injured resident, and the worker's livelihood all press in different directions.

situation_features.relationship: temporary care aide placed through an agency, with residents, relatives, unit staff, and the agency all involved
situation_features.note: public minor injury, written account due within days, transactional request for protective wording; responsibility across the agency-unit supply chain is live but not settled

seed_situation: A front-desk assistant at a fertility clinic is helping with a public information session in the waiting area. A counselor tells the group that an optional, low-cost add-on appointment 'helps most people feel more in control' and does not mention that the clinic's own summary says it has little evidence of improving outcomes. Several patients look relieved and begin asking to book it before they leave. The assistant, who has no clinical authority, is torn between correcting the implication and protecting the group's fragile hope.
why_it_is_hard: Speaking now may cause brief distress and embarrassment, while staying quiet may let patients book a low-cost add-on on an inflated expectation. The later benefit of correction is uncertain, and the cost falls on the patients either way.

situation_features.relationship: front-desk assistant, counselor, and patients in a public clinic session
situation_features.note: the asker has no clinical authority; the issue is an overly optimistic public statement about a low-cost optional service

seed_situation: At a further education college, a mature student on a digital design diploma has been giving a younger classmate detailed notes, extra practice files, and sometimes bus fare after evening classes. The classmate has stopped attending the optional study lab and now waits by the asker's locker for help before each assignment. The asker wants to finish a strong portfolio for a university interview, but feels guilty when they try to work alone.
why_it_is_hard: Being kind offers immediate relief and keeps the friendship easy, but repeated rescue may be teaching the classmate to wait for help and costing the asker the hours needed for their own portfolio; pulling back may restore the asker's focus yet leave the classmate without support and make the asker feel harsh.

situation_features.relationship: fellow students in the same programme
situation_features.note: The asker has no formal responsibility for the classmate, and the help is private rather than part of college policy.
